subject: SNAP retailer stocking standards
title: What are the new SNAP rules for stores? The 2026 stocking standards
answer: Stores that accept SNAP food stamps must now stock at least seven varieties of staple food in each of four categories: protein, grains, vegetables or fruits, and dairy. That is up from three. The USDA rule took effect July 7, 2026, and stores had to comply by Nov. 4, 2026.
body:
The USDA's Food and Nutrition Service published the final rule, "Updated Staple Food Stocking Standards for Retailers in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program," in the Federal Register on May 8, 2026. Stores must carry 28 staple varieties in total, with at least three stocking units of each variety (84 items). At least one variety in three of the four categories must be perishable, up from two categories before. Plant-based proteins count as protein, and plant-based dairy alternatives can count for up to three dairy varieties.

Snacks and desserts such as chips, candy and baked goods do not count as staple foods, and neither do most drinks (milk, certain milk alternatives and 100% juice are exceptions), condiments, sweeteners, spices, cooking oils or butter. Hot or cold prepared foods made in the store do not count either; pre-cut produce does.

The rule applies to stores that qualify under the USDA's "Criterion A." New stores are checked when they apply, and existing stores are checked at reauthorization, which generally happens every five years, though the agency can review a store at any time. A store that fails the standards can be denied or lose its authorization and must wait six months to reapply. The rule sets what authorized stores must carry; it is not a rule about which items recipients may buy or how much they receive.
in_the_news: The Nov. 4, 2026, compliance deadline for the USDA's tougher SNAP retailer stocking standards has just passed.

faq.q: When do the new SNAP store rules start?
faq.a: The rule took effect July 7, 2026, and stores had to comply by Nov. 4, 2026.

faq.q: How many items does a store need to accept SNAP?
faq.a: At least seven varieties in each of four staple categories, 28 varieties in all, with three units of each.

faq.q: Do chips and soda count as staple foods for SNAP stores?
faq.a: No. Snacks, desserts and most beverages are accessory foods and do not count toward the stocking rules.

faq.q: Can a store lose SNAP for not stocking enough food?
faq.a: Yes. It can be denied or lose authorization and must wait six months to reapply.

faq.q: Does the stocking rule change what I can buy with SNAP?
faq.a: This rule sets what authorized stores must stock; it is not a rule about which items recipients may buy.
